certificationCard.description: Accredited Heroku Developer Professionals can demonstrate their skills and knowledge in designing, configuring, building, and implementing on Salesforce Heroku.

keyConcepts.h2: Heroku Developer AP: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Buildpacks, Runtime & Procfile
blocks.body: Heroku detects the language/framework of an app using Buildpacks — Node.js, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, and more are officially supported. Custom Buildpacks extend the detection and build process. The build process: push code → detect buildpack → compile → create slug → deploy to **dynos**. The Procfile defines process types: `web: node server.js` (HTTP), `worker: node worker.js` (background). Multiple process types can run simultaneously. Eco and Basic dynos sleep after inactivity. The `heroku local` command runs the Procfile locally using `.env` for config vars. The AP exam tests how to configure a Procfile for a multi-process app and how to debug a build failure using build logs.

blocks.heading: Config Vars, Add-ons & Environment Management
blocks.body: Config Vars are environment variables set per Heroku app — accessible in code as `process.env.VAR_NAME`. Never hardcode secrets; always use Config Vars. Add-ons extend Heroku apps with third-party services (databases, email, monitoring, logging) — provisioned via `heroku addons:create`. Each add-on sets Config Vars automatically (e.g., DATABASE_URL for Postgres). Add-on plans scale independently from app dynos. The Heroku CLI (`heroku config:set`, `heroku addons`) manages Config Vars and Add-ons. The AP exam tests how to pass secrets to a Heroku app securely, how to provision and configure an add-on, and how to rotate credentials without downtime.

blocks.heading: Heroku Connect & Salesforce Integration
blocks.body: **Heroku Connect** maps Salesforce object records to **Heroku Postgres** tables, syncing data bidirectionally on a configurable schedule. Setup: provision Heroku Connect add-on → authenticate with Salesforce → create mappings (object, fields, direction). Read mappings pull Salesforce data to Postgres. Write mappings push Postgres changes back to Salesforce. Conflict detection handles records modified in both systems simultaneously. The `_hc_lastop`, `_hc_err`, and `isdeleted` system columns track sync status. Connection limits on Salesforce API calls govern sync frequency. The AP exam tests how to configure a Heroku Connect mapping, troubleshoot sync errors, and design for high-volume bidirectional sync within Salesforce API limits.

blocks.heading: Async Jobs, Workers & Message Queues
blocks.body: Background processing on Heroku uses Worker dynos. Job queues (Redis-backed: Bull, Bee-Queue for Node.js; Celery for Python; Sidekiq for Ruby) decouple work submission from processing. Pattern: web dyno enqueues a job → worker dyno processes it asynchronously. This prevents long-running tasks from blocking HTTP responses and allows independent scaling of web vs. worker processes. Scheduled tasks use Heroku Scheduler add-on (cron-like) or clock processes in the Procfile. Dead Letter Queues capture failed jobs for retry or investigation. The exam tests how to architect a job queue for a given throughput requirement and how to handle job failures gracefully.

blocks.heading: Monitoring, Logging & Performance
blocks.body: Heroku Logplex aggregates logs from all Dynos, Router, and **add-ons** into a unified stream — `heroku logs --tail` for real-time viewing. Log Drains forward logs to external services (Papertrail, Datadog, Splunk). Application metrics (response time, throughput, error rate) are visible in the Heroku Dashboard. Dyno metrics show CPU and memory usage — memory leaks cause R14 (memory quota exceeded) errors. R10 (Boot timeout), H10 (App crashed), H12 (Request timeout at 30s) are common Heroku error codes. New Relic, Scout APM, and Datadog add-ons provide application performance monitoring. The exam tests how to diagnose a performance problem using logs and metrics, and how to configure alerting for dyno errors.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Heroku Developer Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Heroku Developer AP exam tests hands-on Heroku development: deploying applications, configuring dynos, working with add-ons, and integrating with Salesforce via Heroku Connect.

blocks.heading: Heroku Deployment Workflow
blocks.body: Know the Heroku deployment flow: git push heroku main, Procfile configuration (web/worker dyno types), buildpack selection (auto-detected or explicit), and how release commands run post-deploy tasks.

blocks.heading: Dyno Configuration & Scaling
blocks.body: Know dyno types (eco, basic, standard, performance), how to scale horizontally (heroku ps:scale web=3) and vertically (dyno size), and how the Heroku Router distributes requests across web dynos.

blocks.heading: Heroku Postgres
blocks.body: Know Heroku Postgres tiers, how to provision a database (heroku addons:create heroku-postgresql), run psql console sessions, create and restore backups, and promote a follower database during failover.

blocks.heading: Heroku Connect Setup
blocks.body: Know how to configure Heroku Connect: creating the connection, mapping Salesforce objects to Postgres tables, configuring sync direction (bidirectional, Salesforce to Heroku, Heroku to Salesforce), and troubleshooting sync errors.

blocks.heading: Config Vars & Add-ons
blocks.body: Know how to manage Heroku config vars (environment variables) for storing credentials, how to provision common add-ons (Redis, SendGrid, Papertrail), and how to use the Heroku CLI to manage your application.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Heroku?
options: A cloud platform for building, running, and managing apps (PaaS)

sampleQuestions.question: Which language/runtime does Heroku commonly support?
options: Node.js, Ruby, Python, Java, and more

sampleQuestions.question: Which role typically pursues Heroku Developer AP?
options: Partners and developers working with Heroku
sampleQuestions.explanation: Partners and developers working with Heroku pursue this credential.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Dyno in Heroku?
options: A lightweight container that runs a single user-specified command
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Dyno is a container that runs a single command on Heroku.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Heroku Config Vars store?
Which Heroku add-on provides managed databases?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Heroku Postgres and Redis are managed add-ons.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Procfile used for?
options: To declare process types (web, worker) and commands
sampleQuestions.explanation: Procfile declares process types and commands.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Heroku feature supports Git-based deployment?
What does Heroku Buildpack do?
options: Compiles and prepares app for execution

sampleQuestions.question: Which Heroku plan supports scaling?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dyno scaling supports web and worker scaling.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Heroku Logs?
options: To view application and system logs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Heroku Logs provide application and system logs.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice applies to Heroku development?
options: Use Config Vars, stateless processes, and 12-factor

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Heroku release?
options: A versioned deployment combining slug and config; each deploy creates a new release
sampleQuestions.explanation: A release is an immutable combination of slug and config; rollbacks revert to prior releases.
